correctness.rationale: The graph, integer parameters and edge deletion are unambiguous. The n=4k+1 deletion is known contractible; the displayed folds reduce its link to one \(C_{6k}\) and thus suspend two \((2k-1)\)-spheres. For \(n=4k+2\), exact fold sequences reduce deletion/link to \((2k+1)K_2\) and \(2kK_2\); the attaching map \(S^{2k-1}\to S^{2k}\) vanishes. The fold witnesses are explicit uniform expressions with bounded residue offsets; exact independent graph construction checked 2320 folds across 70 cases and 4 small homology tests, with the infinite argument relying on the symbolic sequences and classical cofibration/fold results.

value.rationale: Deleting one rung is the minimal natural failure of the symmetry hypothesis of the new 2026 Möbius-ladder classification. Despite the original complexes having one or three top spheres, two consecutive infinite congruence classes of the perturbed graph yield exactly two integral spheres. The fact determines homotopy rather than merely Euler or field Betti data and the explicit fold certificates explain the distinct mechanisms; it is neither an arbitrary finite table nor a special case of the intact-ladder theorem.
